question: The Jain monastic establishments are called as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Basadis**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Jain monastic establishments are called **Basadis**.
 
• Basadis are Jain temples or monasteries, primarily found in Karnataka, India.
 
• They are important centers for religious and cultural activities of the Jain community.
 
• Basadis often house images of Tirthankaras and are places where Jain monks and nuns reside and practice their faith.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aparigraha** is a principle of non-possessiveness in Jainism.
 
• **Svetambara** is one of the two main sects of Jainism, the other being Digambara.
 
• **Tirth** refers to a pilgrimage site in Jainism.
 
• Jainism emphasizes principles such as non-violence (Ahimsa), truth (Satya), and non-attachment (Aparigraha).
 
• Jain monastic life is highly disciplined and involves strict adherence to ethical principles.
